newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Talk of a top as Australian dollar stumbles.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Talk of a top as Australian dollar stumbles.

text.p: Offshore sellers tore 3/4 cent off the Australian dollar Tuesday, snapping important support and possibly putting paid to its recent uptrend.

The currency's five-week-old, four-cent-wide rally came to a schreeching halt overnight as U.S., Swiss, and Chinese selling swamped the market. And it shuddered into reverse this morning when a U.S. investment house forced a break of US$0.7925 support and triggered distressed stop loss selling to a US$0.7889 low.
Importer buying around 79 cents helped steady a few frayed nerves, but dealers reckoned risks were the currency had found a top for the time being and a deeper correction lay in store.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the dollar had found a temporary haven at US$0.7900/05 after recoiling from an early US$0.7925/30 and US$0.7974/79 late here Monday.

"The writing was on the wall when the Aussie couldn't sustain a rally above 80 cents," said one local bank dealer. "It made holders think about the profits they were already sitting on rather than those that might lie ahead."

Once a few started to take profits it encouraged speculators to go short and fuel the correction. "That's what the U.S. house was up to; he's known for coming in heavy when there's a chance of taking out a big level and triggering stops," said one.
"It certainly worked today with breaks of US$0.7925 and US$0.7910 forcing a lot of people to dump their positions."
Chart watchers noted it had also broken an upward sloping trendline which had guided the currency up from last month's US$0.7550 low.
This was seen as a bearish omen perhaps preceding a protracted period of consolidation with US$0.7835 as the immediate floor, although some saw scope for a correction as deep as US$0.7750.
A rise and close above US$0.7960 was needed near term to revive the uptrend and bring the 82 cent target back in sight.
The dollar suffered a similar pullback on the crosses as the market decided it was an opportune moment to take profits on recent hefty gains.

Some direct selling was seen out of Tokyo overnight which grew today when US$/yen took a late tumble and pushed the local dollar down to 97.24/34 yen from 98.54/64 late Monday and a 4-1/2 year high around 98.90 last week.
The broader selloff also lopped 0.5 point off the currency's trade weighted index leaving it at 60.9.
Dealers also looked for a stretch of consolidation here, although favourable yield differentials should underpin the A$.
Australian yields had been on the rise recently after the Reserve Bank said economic prospects were bright enough that another cut in official rates was not warranted for the moment.
Today's, admittedly secondary, data did nothing to change the perceived status quo.

Housing starts for the December quarter jumped 5.9 percent in an expected rebound from the 5.5 percent fall reported for Q3. This was the first quarterly rise since Q4 last year and took annual growth to 2.2 percent after an 11.4 percent dive in Q3. The data added to evidence the housing market had bottomed late last year and was now embarked on a gradual recovery.
Also out were manufacturing input prices for January which showed a surprisingly strong 1.9 percent rise for the month after a 0.2 percent fall in December.
The increase was largely due to rises in domestic prices for oil, milk, wheat and lamb, all of which are volatile and often influenced by seasonal factors rather than simple demand.
In annual terms prices were still down 4.6 percent, largely courtesy of the strength of the dollar last year which kept down import prices.
